name: Gixo
summary: Seven separate AI workspaces (decks, articles, visuals, briefs, proposals, legal drafts and books), each sold on its own plan.
best_for: teams that want one dedicated, source-grounded tool per deliverable (a deck tool, a content tool, a proposal tool) and would rather buy them separately than bend one generic generator into every shape
skip_if: you want a single flat AI subscription covering writing and design together, or you cannot justify stacking three narrow products to cover what one tool does under one price
honest_knock:
Two things about this pricing are worth reading twice.

The first is that seven products means seven subscriptions, and most of them are now per seat. Gixo is priced per deliverable, not per company, and one product's plan does not include the others. A team that needs decks, articles and proposals buys Lumen plus Quill plus Arc: $69 a month for one person at the entry tiers, $133 at the Starter tiers Gixo now recommends, and at least $759 a month for three people on the Professional tiers that add shared review. There is no published bundle price; the only route the page names is procurement, where private offers and multi-product bundles go through review. Ask for that before you subscribe to the second product, not after.

The second is the seat minimums (read 21 October 2026). On 4 October Quill Professional was $79 a month for three seats; it is now $79 a seat with a three-seat minimum, and every tier above the one-seat tiers on Quill, Lumen, Business, Lex and Arc works the same way. The generation allowance behind each tier is still not stated outside Folio's chapter counts, and the first step is steep on Quill: Lite at $10 is pitched at publishing now and then, the next tier is $59. Run the 14-day trial at the volume you actually expect.

pricing.notes: (re-read 2026-10-21 on gixo.ai/pricing in served HTML; the floors are unchanged, but the billing unit changed after our 4 October reading: five of the seven products are now priced per seat with a seat minimum per tier, where on 4 October each tier was one monthly price for a stated number of seats) Gixo is not one product but seven, each bought on its own plan, in USD. Per seat per month, with the annual figure per seat: Quill: Lite $10 (from 1 seat, $90 a year), Starter $59 (from 1 seat, $599), Professional $79 (minimum 3 seats, $799), Business $99 (minimum 5, $999), Enterprise $129 (minimum 10, $1,299). Lumen: Lite $10 ($90), Starter $25 ($250), Professional $45 (minimum 2, $450), Business $55 (minimum 5, $550), Enterprise $99 (minimum 10, $999). Business: Starter $19 ($190), Professional $49 (minimum 3, $499), Business $59 (minimum 5, $599), Enterprise $79 (minimum 10, $799). Lex: Solo Pilot $29 ($261), Solo $99 ($999), Small Firm $149 (minimum 3, $1,499), Growing Firm $179 (minimum 5, $1,799), Marketplace $229 (minimum 10, $2,299). Arc: Starter $49 ($490), Professional $129 (minimum 2, $1,299), Business $149 (minimum 5, $1,499), Enterprise $179 (minimum 10, $1,799). The FAQ says a team can add seats above each minimum. Prism and Folio still charge one price per plan for the seats it includes: Prism Starter $10 (1 seat, $90 a year), Professional $25 (2 seats, $250), Business $45 (5, $450), Enterprise $99 (10, $999); Folio Author $19 for 10 AI-drafted chapters a month and Pro $99 for 50, one seat each, with no annual figure. So the smallest bill on a tier with a seat minimum is the seat price times the minimum: Quill Professional at least $237 a month, Arc Professional $258, Lex Small Firm $447. Generation allowances are not quantified on the page except Folio's chapters. The FAQ still says a no-card 14-day trial with full generation, that continued generation after it needs a paid plan while existing work stays viewable, and that there is no standing unpaid tier. Folio is described three ways: “Monthly book plans” on its card, “14-day trial, no card” in the comparison table, and starting free for planning and import in the introduction. Quill, Lumen, Business, Arc and Lex can also be bought through Microsoft Azure Marketplace, where private offers and multi-product bundles are handled through procurement review.

schema_offer.description: Quill or Lumen Lite per seat, or Prism Starter per plan, per month, the lowest published entry tier (one seat) across seven separately sold products; since October 2026 Quill, Lumen, Business, Lex and Arc are priced per seat with a seat minimum per tier, so Quill Professional costs at least $237 a month (3 seats at $79); Prism and Folio charge one price per plan. Read on the vendor's own pricing page on 2026-10-21.

compare_with.name: Gamma or Beautiful.ai
compare_with.why: Gamma and Beautiful.ai do one job, turn a prompt into a presentable deck, and publish a single per-seat price you can multiply in your head. Gixo spreads the same AI drafting across seven separately priced products covering decks, content, visuals, briefs, proposals, legal work and books, so it reaches further and costs more to assemble. If decks are the whole job, the single-purpose tools are simpler and cheaper; if you want the same draft-review-export flow across several deliverables, that breadth is the thing Gixo actually sells. Verify all current price lists yourself; ours were read on 21 October 2026.

claims.plan: No plan was bought; the 14 day Quill trial was started without a card and the plans page was read up to the Start paid checkout buttons

claims.claim: It's longer than you asked for: about 800 words chosen, 1,159 written.

claims.plan: No plan was bought; the 14 day Quill trial was started without a card and the plans page was read up to the Start paid checkout buttons

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session started the 14 day Quill trial in the account that we made (no card) and had Quill write an article of about 800 words from who.int and cdc.gov. The draft was ready in about three and a half minutes after 8 clicks or inputs, but it came out longer than asked (1,159 words) and the panel To check (3) flagged 6 passages. The sources all carry (n.d.), the WHO source is a report from 2004 on noise and sleep disturbance, and the CDC age bands are missing from the text, although the main figure of seven or more hours is right. The Quill plans are the same as in the dossier (Lite $10, Starter $59, Professional $79, Business $99, Enterprise $129), and checkout charges in euros. Nothing was paid and checkout was not reached. Account and start: we made the Gixo account before the test and our AI assistant ran the test in a tab of our Chrome at about 16:00 (Europe/Amsterdam) on gixo.ai/start-trial. The interface was in English; a cookie banner was answered with Reject all. The dashboard showed the products Accord and Keystone under Your products and Quill under More products with a lock. The dossier audience tested is Content writers drafting long articles from sources. Trial: Start your Quill trial. 14 days, no card. The clock starts when you click below, and each product gets one trial per account. The button Start my 14 days started it; no card was asked for. A banner then said 14 days left in your Gixo Quill trial with a Choose a plan link. The trial is now used for this account (one trial per product). Core action: through Choose the format, pictures and sources the topic was What adults need to know about sleep and health, based on guidance from WHO and CDC, with the format Blog Post, the length Short (About 800 words), the box Only these websites set to who.int and cdc.gov, and pictures on (the default). From the trial button to Start writing it took 8 clicks or inputs. Start writing was clicked at about 16:03:30 and the message Your draft is ready. came at about 16:07, so about three and a half minutes. The progress bar showed Generating text content 20% and Attaching cited sources 90%. Result: the article Sleep and Adult Health: What to Know. The panel To check (3) held three Review cards: It's longer than you asked for (about 800 words chosen, 1,159 written), Quill couldn't finish checking every fact against your sources, and Final source review flagged 6 passage(s) to check against the sources, among them the source list itself, with the labels no supplied source backs it and a source contradicts it. The draft was saved as written and the cards say to check it before you publish. Sources: the paragraph Sources captured during generation lists 10 sources, of which the tester counted 8 from cdc.gov or stacks.cdc.gov and 3 from iris.who.int (these counts do not add up to 10 in the notes). All of them carry (n.d.) with no author or year. The WHO source is a report from 2004 on noise and sleep disturbance (WHO technical meeting on sleep and health: Bonn Germany, 22 to 24 January 2004), not an adult guideline, and the article text itself says that the report does not set that duration target. There were no inline source links in the running text, only the list under Sources at the bottom. The pictures were stock photos marked Photo via Pexels. One source was checked by hand: https://www.cdc.gov/sleep/about/index.html gives adult 18 to 60 years 7 or more hours, adult 61 to 64 years 7 to 9 hours and adult 65 years and older 7 to 8 hours. The article says seven or more hours for all adults and only that sleep needs change with age, so the age bands are missing. The core claim is right and the nuance is missing. The other sources were not checked one by one. Plans read on gixo.ai/products/content?upgrade=true#plans on 18 Nov 2026, in US dollars per seat per month, with the euro price under it: Lite $10 (EUR 9), Starter $59 (EUR 53, Recommended), Professional $79 (EUR 71, Minimum 3, 3 seats selected, Total $237/month), Business $99 (EUR 90, Minimum 5, Total $495/month) and Enterprise $129 (EUR 117, Minimum 10, sold through Azure Marketplace or private offer). The page says You pay in euros: the price under each US dollar price is what checkout charges, set at the European Central Bank reference rate for 13 November 2026. These dollar prices are the same as in the dossier, so the price is UNCHANGED; the euro charge is a detail the dossier does not mention. The plans page was read up to the Start paid checkout buttons and nothing was clicked past them. The billing menu showed No active plans and Manage billing, which was not opened. Cancelling: there is no paid plan, so there was nothing to cancel; the trial ends by itself and existing work stays visible according to the dossier. Not tested: download or export (PDF, Word), publishing, Share, checking all 10 sources one by one (only CDC About Sleep was read), Brand Voice and the other Gixo products. Clean up: the account and the trial stay; the test draft sits in Quill under Your drafts. The own tab was closed and our tab was not touched. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The article came out longer than the length that was chosen. The final review flagged 6 passages and Quill said it could not finish checking every fact, so the writer has to check the draft. The sources carry (n.d.) with no author or year, the one WHO source is a report from 2004 on noise and not an adult guideline, and the CDC age bands are missing from the text. There are no inline source links, only a list at the bottom. The Professional plan has a minimum of three seats, so the smallest bill is $237 a month.
